request: Plan a 150-person Manhattan fundraising gala and check whether we can afford it.

summary_of_changes: Contingency changed from 10% to 22%, moving the projected total from $14,850 to $16,470.
With history, Event Intelligence gave the Events agent 7 evidence-backed constraint(s).
Extra cost of consulting history: $+0.0740 (+1 model calls).
history_constraints: Before signing, compare venue food-and-beverage minimums, per-head pricing, and vendor guarantees in writing, including how minimums interact with guest-count changes.
Use the proposed two-week guest-count lock as a planning requirement to confirm with vendors, and establish a seating-change process before the final deadline.
Create a distinct volunteer-food budget rather than assuming attendee catering covers volunteers.
Have a workable table-payment process ready before the gala rather than making post-event pledge follow-up the default.
Test registration before launch, lock sponsor logos a month before printing, and set auction-item delivery deadlines to reduce rush work.
Bring the catering-risk and donor-experience positions to the board before approving the meal format; the reflections do not establish agreement to cut food or retain it at any cost.
Past reflections report overruns; plan at least 22% contingency.

only_without: No historical event lessons or named past-event records were supplied, so no event-specific lessons can be attributed. The current Manhattan Spring Gala revision applies Finance’s feedback by replacing the unaffordable seated dinner with a reception.
only_with: Butterfly Benefit Dinner (sample): preserve the mission-centered recovery speaker while drafting a shorter formal program. The under-an-hour recommendation reflects individual advice, not documented board consensus.
Butterfly Benefit Dinner (sample): obtain written catering prices and clarify venue minimums and guest-count changes; food costs were a significant source of exposure.
Butterfly Benefit Dinner (sample): collect donations during the event and distinguish pledges from received payments rather than relying on later follow-up.
Butterfly Benefit Dinner (sample): establish earlier operational deadlines and explicitly resolve the tension between meal quality and cost control.

only_without: Offer standard reception tickets, supporter tickets with an additional charitable contribution, and sponsor-hosted guest packages. Set prices only after the board reviews the revenue assumptions and confirms event costs; no ticket prices are supplied.
Seek event and program sponsorships tied to mental health awareness, eating disorder research, and community. Draft clear recognition benefits without promising unconfirmed venue permissions.
Include a brief mission-focused speaker segment followed by an optional paddle raise or direct appeal. Keep messaging supportive and avoid pressure to disclose personal experiences.
Seek in-kind catering, AV, decor, and printing support. Treat these as prospective contributions, not reductions to the computed budget, until confirmed.

Use the supplied low revenue scenario of $34,815.9, base scenario of $49,737, and high scenario of $57,197.55 for sensitivity planning, not as guaranteed income. Track committed sponsorships, ticket receipts, and pledges separately.
only_with: Agree whether fundraising or awareness is the primary objective before committing the budget; track collected payments separately from pledges.

Develop standard, supporter, and sponsored-access ticket tiers. Set prices only after the board reviews the final catering scope, donor experience, and confirmed budget; ticket prices are not supplied.
Seek sponsorship for mission programming, production, and volunteer meals. Request written commitments and distinguish cash sponsorship from in-kind support.
Invite in-kind catering and production support, subject to vendor acceptance and written scope. Do not reduce the supplied budget for unconfirmed donations.
Pair a brief mission-centered speaker segment with a focused paddle raise. Draft the formal program under an hour, recognizing that this is advisory rather than documented board consensus.
Provide a tested, staffed payment table suitable for a reception so guests can complete donations during the event rather than relying on later pledge follow-up.

Use the supplied low $34,815.9, base $49,737.0, and high $57,197.55 revenue scenarios only as planning sensitivities, not guaranteed collections. Their historical basis is a sample dinner and may not transfer to a reception.

Plan for 150 attendees and confirm whether venue capacity includes staff, volunteers, speakers, and vendors.
Agree on a guest-count lock and catering guarantee deadline; neither is supplied.
Verify step-free access, accessible restrooms, seating for guests who cannot stand comfortably, dietary accommodations, and space for a quieter area.
Build a run of show around arrival, passed bites, a speaker, the fundraising appeal, and closing. Confirm AV needs and sound restrictions.
Assign volunteers to check-in, accessibility support, speaker coordination, and donation tracking. Confirm deposit and payment deadlines against available cash.
only_with: Confirm availability for 2027-04-17 before proceeding. Obtain written venue and catering quotes covering minimums, per-head pricing, vendor guarantees, guest-count changes, and all included services.
Have the budget calculator verify at least 22% contingency and a distinct volunteer-food budget before any commitment. The supplied totals do not establish these requirements.
Confirm the proposed two-week guest-count lock with vendors and establish a controlled process for late attendance, seating, and layout changes.
Test registration before launch, lock sponsor logos a month before printing, and set auction-item delivery deadlines if an auction is included.

headlines.without_history: Advance the Chelsea Atelier reception: affordable on current assumptions, subject to quote and cash-flow validation.
headlines.with_history: Proceed with conditional planning for a 150-person Manhattan reception—not a venue commitment.

recommendations.without_history: Recommend a 150-person Manhattan Spring Gala reception at Chelsea Atelier (synthetic), proposed for April 17, 2027. The projected cost is $14,850, with $6,150 upfront. Finance reports that this option passes all four affordability checks. Advance to validation—not booking or spending—because supplier prices, availability, fundraising commitments, and later payment coverage remain unconfirmed.
recommendations.with_history: Chelsea Atelier’s synthetic reception option is affordable in the supplied planning model: projected cost is $16,470, including $2,970 contingency, with $6,150 required upfront. Recommend developing this option for the proposed April 17, 2027 gala, subject to board acceptance of a reception rather than a seated dinner, verified quotes, operational checks, and a payment-and-receipts schedule. Actual affordability remains conditional; projected fundraising is not committed cash.
